original_target.title: A planar compact set with full projections and a nowhere dense triple sum

full_original_statement:
Does there exist a compact set $`K\subseteq[0,1]^2`$ such that every affine line $`L\subseteq\mathbb R^2`$ satisfies

```math
L\cap[0,1]^2\ne\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad L\cap K\ne\varnothing,
```


while

```math
K+K+K=\{x+y+z:x,y,z\in K\}
```


has empty interior in $`\mathbb R^2`$? This sum is compact, so empty interior is equivalent to nowhere density. The incidence condition is equivalent to every orthogonal line projection of $`K`$ being the full corresponding projection of the square.

This is Question 11.3 in the latest arXiv version of [1].

sources.scope_comparison: The actual Question 11.3 states exactly the requested planar compact (3,1,2)-set. The full-projection construction proves a nowhere-dense double sum, and the higher-dimensional l-fold results do not supply dimension two with three summands. Nonempty-interior projections weaken exact full-square projections. No later matching construction, impossibility theorem or complete announcement was found.
